newsitem.title: TURKEY: Motorola, Turkey's Telsim sign $90 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Motorola, Turkey's Telsim sign $90 mln deal.

text.p: Motorola and Turkish GSM operator Telsim signed a $90 million contract to double Telsim's GSM network in Turkey by the end of 1997, the two companies said in a joint news conferecence on Tuesday.
The two companies also agreed to expand the investment to $160 million afterwards to triple Telsim's line capacity.

"This microcellular system to be installed in Telsim's network will be one of the first applications in the world and will help Telsim to raise its service quality while expanding the line capacity," Paul Strzelecki, Vice President of Motorola Europe Cellular Communication, told the conference.
Strzelecki said this investment would help Telsim to rapidly regain its domestic market share which fell sharply due to a conflict with Turk Telekom earlier this year.
"Our target is to increase our market share to 50 percent from current 25 percent," Nur Sakarya, Telsim board member, told the conference.
He said Telsim's market share had stood at between 45-50 percent before the conflict emerged. Turk Telekom and Telsim settled their disputes with a new accord signed in early July.
Motorola will build 500 new GSM stations for Telsim in 1997 under the $90 million, turn-key contract and another 250 stations when the investment is expanded to $160 million.

Sakarya said Telsim's total investments would reach $1 billion next year, including a $500 million licence fee to be paid in a year after the signing of a 25-year licence contract with the government, expected in the first quarter of 1997.
"Our total investment excluding the licence fee will reach $1 billion by the year 2010," he said, adding that Telsim would begin to post profits in three or four years.
Telsim is owned by Rumeli Holding which is run by the Uzan family. The other GSM operator in Turkey is Turkcell.
The government expects to earn a total of $1 billion from the GSM licence deals expected to be signed with Telsim and Turkcell in early 1997. The deals will require them to pay in one year.
